info.title: Hrizzup API
info.description:
Hrizzup's API for bots and AI tools: play-money prediction markets and a Bitcoin perp, with the same calls Hrizzup's website and app use.

**This is the demo, on staging:** play money only, keys that work only here, and data that may be reset (with notice in the changelog). Production's API opens at launch.

- **Public reads need no key** (markets, perps, health) and are kept at the edge for a few seconds. Send them no key: a request with an `Authorization` header is never answered from the edge's copy.
- **Personal calls need a key** (your balance, positions, orders; and, with a trading key, trading and the perp): `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Manifold's `Authorization: Key <key>` works too. Make keys on the sandbox's keys page, signed in.
- **Amounts are exact decimal text** (`"25"`, `"2.5"`), never JSON numbers, and times are ISO 8601 in UTC.
- **Lists page one way:** `limit` (1 to 100, 50 by default) and `cursor`, the `next` of the page before, sent back as it came; `next` is null on the last page.
- **Every refusal has one format:** `{ defined, code, status, message, data }`; a refused input is 400 `BAD_REQUEST` with each problem in `data.issues`.
- **Limits:** 60 requests a minute from each address, 120 personal reads a minute for each key, 30 trades a minute for each account. Past one, 429 with `Retry-After`; the `RateLimit-Policy` and `RateLimit` headers say how much is left.
- **Versioning:** within v1, only additions: new calls, new optional inputs, new fields. Ignore fields you don't know.

agreement.common.one_line.title: One line of plain text
agreement.common.one_line.description: Plain text on one line: no spaces at either end, and no control, direction or other invisible characters (the zero-width joiner inside some emoji is the one exception).

agreement.common.record_id.title: Record ID (UUID version 7, lower case)
agreement.common.record_id.description: A record's own ID. Made once by whoever writes the record, and never changed.

agreement.common.text.title: Plain text, new lines allowed
agreement.common.text.description: Plain text that may run over several lines: no spaces or new lines at either end, and no control (other than the new line), direction or other invisible characters (the zero-width joiner inside some emoji is the one exception).

agreement.common.time.title: Time in UTC, like 2026-11-05T09:30:00Z
agreement.common.time.description: A moment in time, always in UTC, with up to six decimals on the seconds.

agreement.common.web_address.title: Web address starting https://
agreement.common.web_address.description: A public web address. Shown as a plain link; our software never follows it on its own. Its host is written in plain letters, digits, hyphens and dots (an international name in its xn-- form), with no name or password before it, so every language reads the same host from it.

Market.title: Market, format version 1
Market.description: A play-money question about the future. A market is data, not code: it holds its question, outcomes, rules, opening and closing times, the source that settles it and its state, so the engine, trading, balances and settlement work the same for any question. Only Hrizzup creates markets. Each settles in one of two ways: by hand, by a Hrizzup admin, or automatically, by a resolver that reads the named source at the closing moment. There is no outside oracle and no dispute process (PLAN.md section 2).

format.description: Says this record is a market, in format version 1.

question.description: The question people bet on, as shown.

categories.description: The categories whose news shows alongside the market.

kind.description: yes_no: people buy Yes or No. multiple_choice: several outcomes, exactly one of which wins.

outcomes.description: The possible outcomes, in the order shown. Required for multiple_choice, and only there: a yes_no market's outcomes are always Yes and No.

rules.description: How the market settles, in plain words, shown with it: what makes each outcome win, what is read from the source and when, and when the market is cancelled instead.

source.description: The named source that settles the market: what the admin or the resolver reads at the closing moment.

settlement.description: by_hand: a Hrizzup admin settles it from the source, and every settlement is logged (who, when, the outcome and the evidence). automatic: a resolver we choose reads the source at the closing moment and settles it.

closes_at.description: When betting stops: the closing moment, when the source is read.

state.description: draft: being prepared, not taking bets yet. open: taking bets. closed: betting has stopped and the market waits to be settled. settled: paid out. cancelled: every bet returned.

result.description: What won: yes or no, or the winning outcome's code. Only when the state is settled.

cancel_reason.description: Why the market was cancelled, in our own words. Only when the state is cancelled.

settled_at.description: When it was settled or cancelled. Only when the state is settled or cancelled.

updated_at.description: When anything about the market last changed.

apiKey.description: Your API key (`hz_demo_…`), from the sandbox's keys page: read-only or trading. Shown once when made.
